ai.literal: Desire, they say, to all living beings at all times, is the unceasing birth-yielding seed.
ai.translation: They say that desire is the seed that yields unceasing birth to all living beings at all times.
ai.modern: எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் எக்காலத்திலும் முடிவில்லாத பிறப்பைத் தரும் விதை ஆசையே என்று கூறுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet identifies desire as the root cause of the endless cycle of birth and suffering. The word 'அவா' means craving or desire, which acts as a 'வித்து' or seed. Just as a seed inevitably sprouts, desire guarantees that a soul will be reborn ('தவாஅப் பிறப்பு') across all times ('எஞ்ஞான்றும்'). By cutting off this desire, one can stop the cycle of rebirth.

ai.literal: When desiring, one must desire non-birth; further, that, desirelessness by desiring, will come.
ai.translation: If one must desire anything, one should desire not to be born again. That state of non-birth will come by seeking to be free from all desires.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் எதையாவது விரும்பினால், இனி பிறக்காமல் இருப்பதையே விரும்ப வேண்டும். அந்தப் பிறவா நிலை, எந்த ஆசையும் இல்லாமல் இருப்பதையே விரும்புவதால் கிடைக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet plays on the word 'desire' to show how to overcome it. It states that if a person must wish for something, they should wish for an end to the cycle of birth. The second line explains how to achieve this: the state of non-birth is attained simply by desiring 'desirelessness' itself. By making the absence of desire the only goal, all other worldly attachments are severed.

ai.literal: Desirelessness like excellent wealth here is not; there also to that equal is not.
ai.translation: There is no excellent wealth in this world like desirelessness, and there is nothing equal to it anywhere else.
ai.modern: ஆசையின்மைக்கு ஒப்பான சிறந்த செல்வம் இவ்வுலகில் வேறு இல்லை; அவ்வுலகிலும் அதற்கு இணையானது எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet declares that the absence of desire is the greatest possible wealth. It uses the word 'ஈண்டு' (here) to refer to the present world and 'ஆண்டும்' (there) to refer to any other realm or future state. By comparing desirelessness to 'விழுச்செல்வம்' (excellent wealth), it shows that true richness comes from not wanting things, rather than accumulating them. Thus, freedom from craving is presented as an unmatched treasure in any existence.

ai.literal: Purity that-which-is-called desire absence; and that truth if-desired will-come.
ai.translation: What is called purity is the absence of desire. That absence of desire will come if one desires truth.
ai.modern: தூய்மை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது ஆசை இல்லாமல் இருப்பதே ஆகும். அந்த ஆசையற்ற நிலை, உண்மையை நாடினால் தானாகவே வரும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet defines true purity as the complete absence of desire. It then explains how to achieve this pure state. The word 'வாய்மை' here is best understood as truth or reality. By seeking the truth of existence, one naturally sheds false attachments, allowing the absence of desire to follow.

ai.literal: Those who have severed, they will say, are those who have severed desire; others, like that, have not severed.
ai.translation: The wise say that only those who have severed desire have truly severed their bonds. Others have not completely severed them.
ai.modern: ஆசையை முழுமையாக விட்டவர்களையே பற்றற்றவர்கள் என்று அறிஞர் கூறுவர். மற்றவர்கள் வெளிவேடத்திற்காகத் துறந்தாலும், அவர்கள் பற்றுகளை முழுமையாக விட்டவர்கள் அல்லர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true renunciation by focusing on the root cause of attachment. It states that only those who have completely severed 'அவா' (desire) can be called 'அற்றவர்' (those who have severed their bonds). Others, who may have given up external possessions but still harbor desires, have not truly achieved the state of renunciation.

ai.literal: Fearing, if one considers, is virtue indeed; a person, that which deceives, if one considers, is desire.
ai.translation: If one considers what deceives a person, it is desire; and if one considers true virtue, it is to fear that desire.
ai.modern: ஒருவனை வஞ்சிப்பது எதுவென்று ஆராய்ந்தால் அது ஆசையே ஆகும்; எனவே அந்த ஆசையைக் கண்டு அஞ்சுவதே உண்மையான அறமாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet identifies desire as the ultimate deceiver of human beings. The word 'வஞ்சிப்பது' (that which deceives) highlights how desire tricks the mind into endless, destructive pursuits. Because of this inherent danger, the text declares that 'அஞ்சுவது' (fearing desire) is 'அறன்' (virtue itself). The repeated use of 'ஓரும்' (if one considers or examines) invites the reader to reflect deeply on the deceptive nature of desire and the moral necessity of avoiding it.

ai.literal: If one fully severs desire, the unfailing state will come by the way oneself desires.
ai.translation: If one completely severs desire, an imperishable state will come to them in the very way they desire.
ai.modern: ஆசையை முழுமையாக அழித்துவிட்டால், ஒருவன் விரும்புகின்ற வழியிலேயே அவனுக்கு அழியாத நன்னிலை வந்து சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the ultimate reward of eradicating desire. The word 'அவா' means desire or craving, and 'ஆற்ற அறுப்பின்' emphasizes cutting it off completely without any residue. When a person achieves this, 'தவா வினை'—an unfailing or imperishable state of being—is attained. Ironically, by giving up all desires, the supreme state comes to the person exactly in the manner they would wish ('தான் வேண்டும் ஆற்றான்').

ai.literal: Desire to those without, non-existent becomes sorrow; that if exists, unceasingly more and more will come.
ai.translation: Sorrow does not exist for those who are without desire. If desire exists, sorrow will come unceasingly, more and more.
ai.modern: ஆசை இல்லாதவர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் இல்லை. அந்த ஆசை இருக்குமானால், துன்பம் அழியாமல் மேன்மேலும் வந்து கொண்டே இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes a direct cause-and-effect relationship between desire and sorrow. For those who have completely severed desire, suffering ceases to exist. However, if even a trace of desire remains, it acts as a seed from which endless sorrows will continuously multiply and afflict them. The word 'மேன்மேல்' emphasizes the compounding and relentless nature of suffering born from desire.

ai.literal: Joy ceaselessly will-gather, desire called among-sorrow sorrow if-perishes.
ai.translation: If the sorrow of all sorrows called desire is destroyed, joy will gather ceaselessly.
ai.modern: அவா என்று சொல்லப்படும் துன்பங்களிலேயே மிகப்பெரிய துன்பம் அழிந்துவிட்டால், ஒருவருக்கு இன்பம் இடைவிடாமல் வந்து சேரும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet identifies desire as the ultimate source of suffering, calling it the 'sorrow among sorrows' (துன்பத்துள் துன்பம்). It states that if this root cause of misery is completely destroyed, a person will experience uninterrupted joy. The word 'ஈண்டும்' (will gather) implies that true happiness naturally accrues and stays with someone once the destructive force of desire is removed.

ai.literal: Insatiable natured desire if removed, that state itself unchanging nature will give.
ai.translation: If one removes desire, which is insatiable by nature, that very state will grant an unchanging nature.
ai.modern: ஒருபோதும் திருப்தியடையாத இயல்பைக் கொண்ட ஆசையை ஒருவன் ஒழித்துவிட்டால், அந்த நிலையே அவனுக்கு என்றும் மாறாத நிலையான தன்மையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two types of nature. Desire has an insatiable nature, meaning it can never be fully satisfied and constantly shifts. If one completely removes this desire, that very act of relinquishment grants an unchanging nature, a state of permanent peace. The repetition of the word for nature emphasizes how abandoning a restless state naturally leads to a stable one.
